_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY - this is a shape reference, not content. The band edges and the two fixed
encounters below exist to show one of each schema feature; the trainer ids name NOTHING and
are not meant to. Which trainers a run fights, and where they sit, is server content (plan
§2.7 keeps a transcribed roster out of the mod entirely), so no roster ships loaded.
Write your own at data/<your-namespace>/roguelite/trainer_rosters/<name>.json, or shadow this
path from your own datapack to delete this example. ops/gen_roguelite_roster.py generates and
validates these files without booting a server, and can cross-check the ids against an RCT
trainer datapack - which this mod cannot do, since it never sees RCT's registry.
Bands and fixed encounters hold trainer IDS ONLY. What an id MEANS is decided by the
'generated' block at the bottom: an id listed there fights a team built at the encounter from
its signature species, and an id that is not fights its RCT trainer's authored team. Levels
always come from the wave curve.
Any field whose name starts with '_' is ignored, which is where comments go. Every other
unknown field is an error, so a typo is reported instead of silently taking a default.
_authored_for: The schedule this roster's coverage is checked against. Optional - these ARE the defaults, and
are spelled out here only because the block is easy to miss. Change them if your run config
differs, or the loader will report holes for waves you will never reach (or miss real ones).
_bands: Bands are NOT about levels - level scaling is applied to whatever trainer turns up. They exist
because scaling a team's level does not scale its MOVES, EVs or held items, so a team authored
for wave 10 fights like a wave-10 team at wave 150 no matter what level it arrives at.
Trainer bands and boss bands are checked separately, and each set must cover every wave of its
kind in 1..run_length with no gaps and no overlaps. A trainer is drawn from the covering band's
pool by a seeded draw on (run seed, wave), so a resumed run meets the same trainer.
EDITING A POOL RE-POINTS RUNS ALREADY IN PROGRESS, appending included - the draw is scaled by
the pool size, so adding a trainer moves which one some later wave of an existing run will
meet. It does not break those runs; they stay deterministic, they just answer from the new
pool. Listing an id twice doubles its share - that is the only weighting mechanism, and the
absence of a weight field is deliberate.

bands._max_wave: Omitted, so this band is open-ended. Level flattens at 100 from about wave 138, so the last band is where difficulty has to come from the team rather than the curve.

_fixed: Fixed encounters beat the bands AND the interval schedule. Two forms, and they mean different
no "kind"  - replace the trainer on a wave that is ALREADY a trainer or boss wave. On a wild
wave it would never fire, so the loader reports it: that is what catches a wave
"kind"     - PROMOTE this wave to a trainer or boss wave and fight this trainer. This is how
a ladder lands on waves the interval cannot reach, and declaring the kind is you
saying you know the wave is not scheduled as one. A promoted wave is not
catchable, and a promotion to boss takes the boss level multiplier.
The two entries below are examples of each form, NOT a schedule. Authoring the schedule is a
content decision and is deliberately left undone.

fixed._note: Wave 50 is already a boss wave, so this only pins WHICH boss.

_note: Wave 182 is a wild wave under 5/10. "kind" promotes it - without that this entry would
never fire. This trainer has NO generated entry below, which is deliberate: an Elite Four
member is exactly the fight worth authoring by hand. A generated team is uniform by nature.

_generated: Trainers whose TEAM is generated at the encounter from their signature species, rather than
fought as authored. The trainer id must still name a real RCT trainer - the NPC, its name, its
skin, its bag and its AI all come from there. Only the team is replaced.
A slot is one party position and its alternatives; an alternative is one species' evolution
LINE, base form first. Which alternative is a seeded pick on (run seed, wave), so a trainer
differs between runs and is identical on a resumed one; which STAGE comes from the wave.
A stage is a Cobblemon properties fragment, not just a species id - a regional form is an
ASPECT in Cobblemon ('cobblemon:corsola galarian' is Ghost, 'cobblemon:corsola' is Water), and
getting that wrong is invisible until somebody notices the types are off.
'weight' exists for branching species: Tyrogue becomes three lines, and without weights a slot
meant as a coin flip between two species would quietly become one-in-four for the other one.
'filler' is only used when the band's party size is bigger than the number of signature slots.
No filler means a band asking for six gets four - a smaller party, not an invented one.
THE ONE ENTRY BELOW IS AN EXAMPLE, NOT CONTENT. Generate real ones with
ops/gen_pokerogue_roster.py, into a SERVER-SIDE datapack - never into this mod (plan 2.7).

generated._note: Shape reference only. 'example_trainer_a' is the id used in the early trainer band above.

signature._note: PokeRogue writes this slot as [OMANYTE, KABUTO] - one or the other, per run.

_generation: The dials generation reads. Optional - everything below IS the default, spelled out because the
block is easy to miss, EXCEPT held_items which ships empty.
party_size: 4 early, 5 mid, 6 late. This is a difficulty lever, not a detail: levels flatten at
100 from about wave 138, so party size is one of the few dials still turning up there.
evolution: stage_waves are the intermediate steps; fully_evolved_from is PokeRogue's own rule.
A line shorter than the schedule is clamped, so a two-stage line is already final where a
three-stage one is halfway.
held_items: WHICH items is content, so nothing ships. With no tiers, generated trainers hold
nothing. 'chance' is per Pokemon; 'count' is how many draws one Pokemon gets (Cobblemon holds
ONE item - the extra draws buy a higher hit rate, not a stack); 'boss' filters by wave kind and
may be omitted to match both. The two tiers below are an example of the shape.
boss_shields: PokeRogue's segmented boss HP bar. 'shields' shields split the Pokemon's HP into
shields+1 chunks; no single hit may carry it past a chunk boundary, and each break raises a
random stat one stage. Boss waves ONLY, whatever min_wave says. Ships empty for the same reason
held_items does - which waves are walls is a difficulty curve, and that belongs to the server.
It costs the held item slot: a shielded Pokemon carries no other item, because the shields ARE
its power. 'shields' is 1..5 and the ceiling is not taste - there is one held-item script per
count, so a 6 is an item Showdown does not have and the boss would fight unshielded. 'members'
is how many of the party are shielded, counted from the FRONT (signature slot one, which is
where PokeRogue puts a leader's ace). Unlike everything else here it is NOT a seeded draw:
wave 100 must be the same wall for everybody.

held_items._note: EXAMPLE. Boss waves from 80 on, two draws each at 40% - about two thirds hold something.
EXAMPLE. Everything else from wave 30 on, one draw at 20%.

_boss_shields: EXAMPLE. Highest passed min_wave wins, so the order written here does not decide anything.
This ramp gives the first shielded boss at wave 50 and the last at 150, which is roughly
PokeRogue's own shape at our run length.
